original.target_description: Related target outcome located: ANCOVAs of correct face-location identifications divided by correct plus incorrect identifications, age covariate. One Helsinki-recruited sample is reported, not a Japanese or American sample. Separate paranormal-believer/skeptic and religious/non-religious comparisons are printed; supplied locator does not distinguish them.

n.sample_role: No analytic n for the country-specific target established. Related analyses use upper/lower quartile groups; generic study N=47 is not the target analytic n.
n.exclusions: Originally 73 recruited; 47 included overall; upper/lower belief quartiles retained for group analyses (19 paranormal believers/20 skeptics; 20 religious/19 nonreligious).
n.quote: Only those belonging to the upper and lower quartiles (25%)

replication.target_description: Study 1B, American sample: simple linear regression of mean perceived face-likeness ratings over 35 images on continuous religiosity. This is not identification of predefined face-like regions or a believer-group comparison as described in the supplied neutral locator.

n.sample_role: American participants included in the simple linear regression after exclusions
n.exclusions: Six of 100 recruited participants excluded using the a-priori criterion. Criterion: extreme slider values (1, 50, 100) on at least 95% of test trials and choosing 6 (do not wish to respond) for importance of religion, as worded in the paper. Three practice trials excluded.

notes:
Replication title verified against the supplied reference. The authors explicitly describe successful replication, but the supplied neutral target identifies a detection/group-membership test whereas the actual replication reports face-likeness ratings regressed on continuous religiosity; target_match is therefore false. Original full text unavailable after DOI/publisher, Unpaywall, OpenAlex, CiteSeerX and ResearchGate routes; no secondary-source original values substituted. Cached replication text is the frozen web-tool full-HTML parse with line numbers (includes all relevant methods, results and discussion).
Source follow-up: The requested American sample is absent from this primary paper. No unique original contrast can be selected from the supplied believer-group wording: paranormal vs. skeptic gives partial eta-squared .143, F(1,36)=6.01, p=.019; religious vs. nonreligious gives partial eta-squared .127, F(1,36)=5.26, p=.028. These are contextual candidates only, not assigned target statistics. Rendered primary PDF p. 4 visually checked; canonical TXT has an OCR control character in place of eta; evidence quotes preserve its glyph verbatim. Explicit ellipses omit interleaved text. Original side marked done/target_match false rather than falsely declaring paper unavailable.
